messages:
anika: FYI I opened a docs PR for a Dedicated capacity quick-migration guide — focuses on onboarding reserved pools, per-tenant quota examples, autoscale cooldowns, and SLA wording. link: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2432 Please do quick copy + snippet sanity checks.

mike: @anika reading it now. Can you add a concrete tenant-label example and a minimal autoscale policy snippet (cooldown + scale-up windows)? reviewers skim for examples first. :eyes:

sara: pushed a tiny Python SDK snippet to the PR thread, but not sure about param names. current snippet: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$API_KEY")
resp = client.dedicated.provision(tenant_id="acme", pool_type="reserved", size_gpus=2)
print(resp)
```
Can someone confirm `size_gpus` param exists in the latest client?

docsbot: CI: docs-lint passed. linkcheck: 1 broken link found -> old terraform example (https://github.com/redwood/terraform-examples/blob/master/dedicated/reserved_pool.tf) returned 404 (lines ~78-90).

josh: I'll fix the TF link in the PR and add a note about preemption semantics. Also flagging isolation wording — current draft says "isolated by tenant" which could be misread. Suggest: "per-tenant reserved pools provide compute isolation; preemption only applies to burst capacity and non-reserved tenants."

anika: good call. Also need stronger SLA language — current sentence is vague ('best effort'). Two quick options: 1) "99.9% monthly uptime for Dedicated reserved pools with defined rollback/fallback policy" or 2) "SLA with latency and availability targets during committed capacity windows, with automatic fallback to compatible model variants." Which do we prefer?

mike: I like option 1 for the handbook line, but include option 2 in the runbook (fallback behavior). Suggest edit: replace "best effort" -> "SLA-backed with defined fallback policy (see /docs/playbooks/dedicated-fallback)"

sara: confirmed the SDK param names — `size_gpus` was from an older branch. Updated snippet to: ```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$API_KEY")
resp = client.dedicated.create_reservation(tenant_id="acme", gpus=2, region="us-west-2")
print(resp)
```
Also added a short JS example in case product teams copy it.

josh: added clarity on isolation + preemption lines and updated TF link to the new repo path. I also expanded the autoscale example to show cooldown window: ```yaml
autoscalePolicy:
  scaleUpCooldown: 60s
  scaleDownCooldown: 300s
  maxBurstInstances: 2
```

anika: perfect. Two remaining asks before merge: 1) someone from legal sign-off on SLA phrasing, 2) confirm the playbook link exists or add a redirect rule. I'll ping legal and infra. If both green, I'll merge midday.
mike: I'll take infra for the playbook redirect.
sara: pinged legal (cc @legal). leaving small copy nit: change 'tenant' -> 'tenant (account)' for clarity in onboarding steps.
anika: thanks team — assigning owners in the PR description: docs (anika), infra (mike), SDK (sara), ops (josh). plan: merge after legal + infra OKs. Closing checklist added to PR description. :white_check_mark:
